excerpt: What crash data shows about motorcycle collisions on Dorchester Road, the manoeuvres behind them, and who is usually at fault.
keyTakeaways: Dorchester Road in North Charleston is a hazardous corridor for motorcyclists. Left-turn collisions are behind roughly 42% of fatal two-vehicle motorcycle crashes nationally (NHTSA). Heavy truck traffic, limited sight lines, and speeds above 45 mph drastically reduce survival odds. South Carolina does not require helmets for riders 21 and older (S.C. Code § 56-5-3660). Riders can recover damages if less than 51% at fault. The 3-year statute of limitations (S.C. Code § 15-3-530) governs most injury claims.

faqs.question: Why is Dorchester Road so dangerous for motorcyclists?
faqs.answer: It combines high speeds, heavy truck traffic and unprotected left-turn intersections. Cement mixers, dump trucks and construction vehicles share the corridor, and the Forest Hills Drive, Bacons Bridge Road and Ashley Phosphate junctions all follow the same pattern.

faqs.question: What is the left-turn problem in motorcycle crashes?
faqs.answer: Nationally, left-turning vehicles cause 42% of fatal motorcycle crashes according to NHTSA data. A driver scans oncoming traffic, fails to register the motorcycle's smaller visual profile, judges it as farther away, and turns directly into its path.

faqs.question: How much time does a rider have to react?
faqs.answer: Very little. At 50 mph a rider facing a vehicle turning across their path has less than 2 seconds to react. That is why these collisions are so often fatal even when the rider does everything right.

faqs.question: Does not wearing a helmet affect my claim in South Carolina?
faqs.answer: South Carolina law requires motorcycle operators and passengers under age 21 to wear an approved helmet (S.C. Code § 56-5-3660). State law does not impose that helmet requirement on riders age 21 or older. Talk with an attorney about how the facts of your crash apply to your claim.

faqs.question: What should a family do after a fatal motorcycle crash on Dorchester Road?
faqs.answer: Act before the scene evidence is gone. Signal timing data, vehicle event data and independent witnesses all become harder to obtain quickly, and a lawyer can preserve them while the family deals with everything else.
